cells.tense: The sight is here now and the pen is in your hand.
cells.ask: Name out loud the whole shape of one thing you are in the middle of, then let a day pass without touching it.
cells.core:
You can take in the whole of something without stepping out of it. That is the rare part. Most people get the view or the room, one at a time, and you have both — which is why you say the true thing at the table instead of the safe thing.

Feeling runs alongside the sight, at ordinary size. The whole span of what is felt comes to you without becoming a flood to survive. There is nothing here to fix. What this can feed next is quieter company — sitting with what you know while it settles, and letting someone else arrive at their own pace without your hand on the wheel.
cells.sheetLine: You take in the whole of it and stay inside it.
cells.verb: seeing the whole span of what is felt
cells.place: the room where the pattern shows itself whole

cells.tense: You are watching for an ending that has not arrived yet.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you have been waiting to call finished and put down a first step toward it today.
cells.core:
You keep holding out for the whole picture before you move. Somewhere ahead the thing will be complete and you will finally know what to do, and you are living there — so nothing here gets called done, and you read meaning into every fragment as if the last piece were already on the table.

That pressure has a cost. You strain to see a shape still forming, and the strain is part of what keeps it from settling. Start smaller than the waiting. When you choose one concrete direction from where you actually stand, the picture stops having to be finished before you can act.
cells.sheetLine: You want the ending before you will start.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you.
cells.ask: Do one small thing today you have not done before, with no plan attached to it.
cells.core:
You know how to feel a thing whole — you did it once and it went somewhere painful, so you stopped arriving. Now you look at your own life from the hallway. You can describe the pattern from outside it, and you are not in it while you do.

The ability is still there. What went quiet is the willingness to be a person inside the picture, and pushing feeling back into that gap will not work — trying harder is what emptied it. What refills it comes from the side, through something new and unplanned. One small thing draws you back into the room, and the sight follows on its own.
cells.sheetLine: You see your life whole without standing in it.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you are already writing in.
cells.ask: Say plainly what you think is fair in one situation, out loud, before you have worked out how to say it.
cells.core:
You already read the whole thing — where it is going, who is carrying what, what is owed and by whom. You do that quickly and you do it well. But you describe it as though the situation were simply true on its own, as if you had not just weighed it. The reading happened. The open claim did not.

What runs underneath is a plain sense of what is right, and it is doing the work whether or not you name it. Saying it out loud is not a verdict on anyone. It is admitting, once, that the sense of what is fair came from you.
cells.sheetLine: You already see what is fair. You just have not said so.
